subject: Temporary twilight on-call coverage & SLA credit/deferral request
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme-retail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: support coverage this weekend?

Hi Hannah,

We're expecting increased traffic for a storewide promotion this Saturday (06/12). Our platform team is worried about the 30m P1 response SLA during the twilight hour (18:00-22:00 PDT) — we have a planned data migration that may bump error rates. Can Redwood confirm on-call coverage and options if response latency spikes?

If Redwood can't guarantee the 30m window across that twilight period, we'll need to know whether an SLA deferral or credit is available so our SREs can plan fallbacks. Can we get that confirmation by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Chen
Head of Site Reliability, Acme Retail

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: support coverage this weekend?

Thanks for the heads-up, Lisa — appreciate the lead time. High level: we want to avoid SLA impacts but we also have a temporary twilight-coverage gap next week due to two engineers out on leave. I'm copying the on-call lead (Dylan) and operations (Jonas) so we can map mitigations.

Immediate plan I'm proposing:
- Triage: adopt a temporary 'twilight secondary' from our Dedicated pool between 18:00-22:00 PDT for 06/12.
- Escalation: add a direct on-call escalation line to Redwood Engineering (pager + phone) with an agreed 45-minute P1 response target for that window only.
- Fallback: pre-authorize a single-minute autoscale burst for dedicated nodes tied to the route serving your traffic during the migration.
- Financial: if we miss the standard 30-minute P1 SLA during that window, Redwood proposes a pro-rated SLA credit capped at one week's invoice. We can provide detailed wording for contracts.

Attachments: I attached a proposed rotations spreadsheet and a draft routing doc. Please review and confirm whether the 45-minute contingency and the proposed credit cap is acceptable, and I will escalate for leadership sign-off.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: support coverage this weekend?

Thanks Hannah. Quick technical notes from on-call:
- We can enable the twilight secondary routing and tie it to prefix caching to reduce token generation latency for the busiest endpoints.
- The 45-minute P1 response is feasible operationally for that 4-hour window on 06/12 if we pre-authorize the burst capacity and the limited exception.
- We also recommend a temporary increase in retention for detailed traces during the migration window (48h) so post-incident analysis is actionable.

I've updated support-rotations.xlsx with who would be on-call and the backup chain. Jonny, can you confirm capacity for the Dedicated pool burst (one additional node group) and routing changes?

Dylan
Senior On-call Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: support coverage this weekend?

Confirmed capacity and routing notes:
- Dedicated pool: can spin up the one-node-group burst, will be ready 90 minutes after approval.
- Canary routing doc (proposed-canary-routing.docx) includes the safe knob to route 20% of traffic initially and ramp to 100% over 30 min.
- Trace retention: ops can increase retention to 48h; note there will be an additional telemetry cost (rough estimate attached).

Next steps (please respond to all):
1) Lisa — please confirm you approve the 45-minute contingency for 06/12 twilight and accept the proposed SLA credit cap (one week).
2) Acme procurement — please sign the SLA-exception-form so we can trigger the Autoscale burst by Friday EOD. Doc link included.
3) Redwood leadership: Marissa/Ben — we need sign-off on the exception and the credit cap. If you approve, please reply and I'll submit for billing/finance routing.

Jonas
VP, Infrastructure Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: support coverage this weekend?

I reviewed the plan and approve the temporary exception with conditions:
- Exception window: 06/12/2027 18:00-22:00 PDT only.
- SLA adjustment: P1 response target extended to 45 minutes for that window; all other times remain at standard SLA.
- Credit: pro-rated credit up to one week's invoice if we miss the P1 target during the exception window — billing to finalize exact calculation with Finance.
- Runbook: must include immediate fallback routing and a single designated engineering lead to be paged if latency > 3000ms for 10 consecutive minutes.

Ben, please coordinate the billing credit calc with Finance and Procure team. Hannah, draft a short client-facing note (one paragraph) that we can include in the SLA-exception-form and send to Acme. Once Procurement signs the form, we will enable the burst and the routing.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
